| Field | Value |

## Problem

The release names twelve download targets: profiles × formats ×
architectures. Pick once, correctly, and by role. The set must carry
enough tooling for the work. The set must not carry gigabytes that
never run. No desktop belongs on a box that only an agent touches.
Choosing a profile IS choosing the image. Make the choice a decision,
not a guess.

## Solution

Match the role to the profile. The image-matrix table then names the
exact artefact and its size budget:

| Profile | Carries | Choose it when |
|---|---|---|
| `minimal` | the CORE substrate — kernel, base userland, hardening, safety defaults, desktop, CLI & menu engines; no tool categories enabled (categories are added declaratively later) | learning the system, building a hardened base, or enabling a known exact set |
| `redteam-ai` | the AI red-team lab scope — ATTACK core plus its OPS/DEFENCE pairings | the cookbook's scanning and pair recipes, or LLM red-team engagements |
| `full` | the complete live catalogue ("kali-everything" lab scope) | the live demonstrator, or every category present for exploration |
| `headless-agent` | base + CLI only, no desktop; the qcow2 grows at first boot | an automation host or an agent-operated box (O-7 grants apply) |

The budget table (from the declared build matrix — every artefact's
budget is enforced by construction):

| Target (`nix build .#<ref>`) | Profile | System | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kailash-images-qemu-minimal` / `-iso-minimal` | minimal | x86_64 | ≤4 GB |
| `kailash-images-qemu-redteam-ai` / `-iso-redteam-ai` | redteam-ai | x86_64 | ≤8 GB |
| `kailash-images-qemu-full` / `-iso-full` | full | x86_64 | ≤10 GB |
| `kailash-images-qemu-headless-agent` / `-iso-headless-agent` | headless-agent | x86_64 | ≤1.5 GB |
| `kailash-images-…-aarch64-minimal` (qemu + iso) | minimal | aarch64 | ≤4 GB |
| `kailash-images-…-aarch64-headless-agent` (qemu + iso) | headless-agent | aarch64 | ≤1.5 GB |

Which profile for which cookbook section:

| Cookbook section | Fits profile | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Scanning | `redteam-ai` | the profile carries the a-02 scanner stack (garak…) |
| Attack–defence pairs | `redteam-ai` | the pair thesis uses the OPS target + ATTACK probe (pair recipes over non-shipped postures read the module per release) |
| Ops | `redteam-ai` or `full` | serving (o-04/o-02) ships with the lab scope |
| Administrator | any — `minimal` is the simplest start | admin recipes act on the base system, not a category |

On the booted system, confirm the choice the release declares:

```bash
kailash profile list
```

Expected output shape (one row per profile, TAB-separated):

```
<name>	<layers-summary>	<description>
```

## Discussion

- **The profile is baked into the image name:** a release asset reads
  `kailash-<tag>-kailash-<profile>.<ext>`. The profile pick happens at
  download, not at boot (or pull the matching flake ref). That is why
  this recipe is a download-time decision, not a post-boot one.
- **Categories give finer precision:** between `redteam-ai`
  and `full`, prefer the former unless the complete catalogue is the
  goal. Anything narrower comes as a declarative category enablement +
  rebuild (see [Enable the first category](first-category.html)). The
  category modules are the same modules the profiles use.
- **Data packs are never part of the choice:** wordlists, SDR and
  other corpora use opt-in `kailash-data.*` derivations. The packs
  stay excluded from every default image by construction. No profile
  carries them, and no profile choice can pull them in (see
  [Refresh wordlists and data packs](../admin/data-packs.html)).
- **Safety posture is identical across profiles:** the double-key
  lab-mode gate and the `requires-target` refusals are properties of
  the manifest rows and the base safety module. The posture never
  depends on the chosen profile — `full` is not "more dangerous",
  only "more present".
- **The aarch64 picture:** the arm slice carries the arch strategy
  (x86 hosted builds, local arm builds on Apple Silicon).
  `redteam-ai`/`full` aarch64 rows land with the KA-36 slice-2 sweep.
  Check the release's own artefact table before planning an arm lab.
- **`headless-agent` grows:** the qcow2 budget is the boot-time floor.
  The store grows as the agent enables categories and rebuilds.
  Budget the host disk, not only the download.
